items.title: Traffic speed and acoustic context shape urban soundscape perception
items.summary: In a virtual urban park, 34 participants rated 30 km/h traffic as more pleasant and less eventful than 50 km/h traffic across three acoustic contexts. The context also affected both soundscape dimensions, while the measured difference in perceived workload was not significant.

items.title: Natural soundscaping shows short-lived physiological benefits
items.summary: A controlled field experiment added natural sounds to a traffic-exposed rooftop break area. Working adults in the intervention group showed higher heart-rate variability after the visit and into early sleep that night, but the difference was no longer evident the next morning.

items.title: Symmetry breaking creates directional acoustic interface states
items.summary: An acoustic metagrating experiment realised a Jackiw–Rebbi interface state produced by spontaneous symmetry breaking. The reported surface propagation combined a constant phase jump with highly directional radiation, illustrating a route to robust wavefront control in acoustic devices.

items.title: KTH upgrades its sound and vibration laboratory
items.summary: KTH is modernising the Marcus Wallenberg Laboratory with a modular anechoic chamber and a larger reverberation room, expanding capacity for absorption, transmission, sound-generation, and noise-control measurements.
